title: Stable pin resolution canonicalizer: deterministic mapping from tag/semver to commit hash and profile
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem statement:
Teams and customers pin models using tags (eg. 'stable', 'rlhf-v1'), semver ranges (eg. '>=1.2.0 <2.0.0'), and commit hashes. The current resolution path in the control plane is underspecified for overlapping selectors and for tags that move (mutable tags). This causes non-deterministic runtime behavior, surprising rollouts, and hard-to-reproduce performance regressions.

Objective:
Design and implement a deterministic canonicalizer service and SDK guidance that resolves any user-supplied selector (tag, semver, commit hash, alias) to an immutable canonical reference (release-hash + profile snapshot) used by runtime routing and billing. The canonicalizer should: 1) be deterministic and strongly ordered; 2) emit observable audit records for resolution decisions; 3) preserve backward compatibility with existing client pin surfaces; 4) provide helpful errors and migration hints to SDK callers; 5) enable safe rollouts and fallbacks at runtime.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Canonicalizer resolution precedence matrix (explicit commit > semver range > exact semver > annotated tag alias > moving tag)
- Translation rules for semver ranges to best-fit release-hash with stability window heuristics
- Tag alias expiry and timestamped resolution to make tag pins reproducible
- SDK behavior changes: synchronous resolution vs. lazy runtime resolution and clear error codes
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalizer service exposes API /resolve that accepts selector and returns canonical_release_hash and profile_id and resolution_metadata
Resolution is deterministic: same selector + timestamp returns identical canonical_release_hash until a published release is replaced (immutable releases are preferred)
SDKs include helper utilities: resolveSelectorSync(selector) and resolveSelectorWithFallback(selector, fallback_policy)
Control plane writes audit log entries for every resolution with reason, precedence step, and linked release artifacts
Backward-compat tests ensure older client pin syntaxes still resolve, and there is a migration warning in SDKs when behavior changes
Performance: canonicalizer median p99 latency < 30ms for cached lookups and < 200ms uncached; throughput 2000 rps per replica
design_notes: Precedence matrix: 1) commit hash (full or prefix) -> resolves immediately if artifact exists; 2) exact semver (1.2.3) -> map to release with that exact tag; 3) semver range -> pick highest non-prerelease matching release, prefer releases with 'stable' profile for production customers; 4) annotated tag (tag@timestamp or tag:profile) -> resolve to nearest release at/after timestamp with matching profile; 5) floating tag (eg. 'latest' or 'stable') -> canonicalize to (tag, resolution_timestamp) pair and return resolved release-hash plus expiry TTL
Stability window: for semver ranges prefer releases older than 48 hours for production by default, unless 'force' flag is provided. This reduces surprise immediate roll forward after a new release.

Auditability: each resolved object carries 'resolved_by' field (canonicalizer version), 'resolved_at' timestamp ISO8601, 'precedence_step' string, and 'evidence' list of artifact refs (release-hash, manifest URL). These will be stored in the control plane events table and surfaced in Console per-pin history.

SDK contract: resolveSelectorSync will attempt a cached local mapping, optionally warm by calling /resolve on startup. If network unavailable, SDK returns a clear RETRYABLE_RESOLUTION_ERROR with guidance. We'll add backcompat layer that accepts legacy pins (old 'pin_id' field) and maps to selectors.

Runtime fallback matrix: if runtime cannot find artifact for canonical release-hash, it can fallback according to the client's fallback_policy: none (error), policy 'compatible-rollback' (choose previous release in same major semver with same profile), policy 'graceful-degrade' (switch to CPU-compatible quantized variant).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Spec and tests: finalize precedence matrix and write canonicalizer contract; unit + integration tests for semantics
Phase 2 - Service: implement /resolve in control plane, add caching layer with TTL and invalidation hooks on publish
Phase 3 - SDKs: add resolve helpers, deprecation warnings for legacy pin fields, and add clear error surface for clients
Phase 4 - Console & Auditing: wire per-pin history UI and exportable audit CSV; integrate with Rollouts (canary) to use canonical references
Phase 5 - Monitoring & SLA: add metrics (resolution latency, cache hit rate, mismatch incidents) and set alerting
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Tags move frequently causing churn. Mitigation: timestamped canonicalization + TTL to ensure reproducible pins and warn on high-churn tags
Risk: Increased latency for uncached resolution. Mitigation: aggressive caching, client-side warm-up, and fallback policies
Risk: Backward compatibility break for edge-case legacy pins. Mitigation: compatibility layer and a migration job that annotates older pins with resolved hashes
Risk: Audit volume growth. Mitigation: retention policy and optional sampling for low-sensitivity customers
sdk_notes: JavaScript/TypeScript SDK will expose: resolveSelector(selector: string, options?: { timestamp?: string, preferStable?: boolean }): Promise<{ releaseHash: string, profileId: string, resolvedAt: string, reason: string }>
Python SDK will mirror API but add convenience helper resolve_or_raise(selector) that raises detailed ResolutionError with .code field and .migration_hint
All SDKs will surface deprecation warnings when a customer is using floating tags without explicit timestamp or TTL
test_plan: Unit tests for precedence rules (commit vs semver vs tag) with mocked artifact store
Integration tests: publish new release, assert semver range resolves to correct release after stability window, then after window passes ensure consistent behavior
Chaos test: simulate artifact deletion and verify fallback_policy behaviors at runtime
Cross-version compatibility tests: older SDK pins resolve to canonical hashes in control plane and runtime honors mapping
